propositions: test_rendered_output_is_byte_identical_to_the_landed_renderer kills its pytest-xdist worker on macOS py3.13 because its monolithic loop over 884 corpus units takes 91.6s idle and 504.8s under CPU contention, exceeding CI's 300s per-test timeout
pytest-timeout with --timeout-method=thread calls os._exit(1) from a timer thread when the budget expires, terminating the worker outright without traceback instead of failing the test cleanly
the test's unbounded serial cost (1768 pandoc spawns in a single test function) means corpus growth extends wall-clock time indefinitely rather than adding independent cases

chunking the 884 units into fixed-size batches with parametrization bounds per-test cost by construction, letting xdist distribute work across workers and leaving headroom under the 300s guard even at 5.5x load inflation
a coverage guard test (test_the_equivalence_chunks_cover_every_renderable_unit) asserts all chunks reassemble to the full corpus and total >= 100 units, preventing silent unit drops
the fix maintains byte-identity checking (_EQUIVALENCE_STRIDE=1, real pandoc on both sides) without raising timeout, adding retry markers, or asserting wall-clock time
